title: Understanding of a product/service system design
observation: The article rejects the null of independence between strategy/PSS-dimension categories in its protocol-analysis utterance tables using chi-square tests, reporting p < 0.01. It reports 1450 coded utterances from one PSS design episode.
limits: Null of statistical independence is not the same as a prior directional design theory prediction; one episode does not establish generality, causal identification, or independent replication; potential dependence among utterances requires methodological evaluation.
followup: Check table construction, independence assumptions and whether tested categories/analyses were prespecified; trace later independent reuse.

title: Uncertainty Driven Action (UDA) model
observation: Authors synthesize prior design activity literature and identify three propositions described as concrete claims intended for future empirical testing; discussion starts at PDF page 31.
limits: Stating a proposition for future testing is not actual testing, validation, replication, a multi-group sustained program, or empirical support for that proposition.
followup: Transcribe each exact proposition with page and see whether later independent studies operationalize, test, revise or reject it.

title: Design Thinking as a Master Idea
observation: Authors explicitly interpret Design Thinking as a master idea and rationalized myth; PDF pages 11-13 discuss legitimacy sustained by belief in effectiveness, generalized applicability and organizational networks rather than documented effects.
limits: An argument about legitimation is not by itself a causal, representative demonstration that all design commissions were predetermined or that all design research is invalid.
followup: Check actual empirical sources behind the claims; distinguish design management discourse from disciplinary evidence tests.

title: Supporting and understanding students' collaborative reflection-in-action during design-based learning
observation: Reports a field trial of the ReflectionSchema tool with 13 groups of students. Methods report a class of 28 students, 204 videos captured and 134 retained for analysis; final discussion flags single-school context and limited transferability.
limits: One class and a qualitative/quantitative pilot do not demonstrate independent validation or causal effect; interpretation depends on exact design, comparisons and outcome definitions.
followup: Read instrument and analytic methods, check exclusions/denominators and any baseline or control group before counting H3 or C2.

title: Designing learning technology collaboratively: Analysis of a chatbot co-design
observation: Describes action research with questionnaires/workshops and discusses concrete conflicts about student privacy, monitoring and who controls data in the chatbot design process.
limits: Discourse about an ethical dilemma is not evidence of effective institutional sanctions, implemented protections, or avoided harm.
followup: Check whether recorded privacy concerns produced a documented revision to implementation and what evidence supports this.
